sourceChecks.text: Ozem the sixth, and David the seventh;
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: Now these were the sons of David, who were born to him in Hebron: the firstborn, Amnon, of Ahinoam the Jezreelitess; the second, Daniel, of Abigail the Carmelitess;
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: All these were the sons of David, in addition to the sons of the concubines; and Tamar was their sister.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: at Beth Marcaboth, Hazar Susim, at Beth Biri, and at Shaaraim. These were their cities until David’s reign.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: These are they whom David set over the service of song in the LORD’s house after the ark came to rest there.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: The sons of Tola: Uzzi, Rephaiah, Jeriel, Jahmai, Ibsam, and Shemuel, heads of their fathers’ houses, of Tola; mighty men of valor in their generations. Their number in the days of David was twenty-two thousand six hundred.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: All these who were chosen to be gatekeepers in the thresholds were two hundred twelve. These were listed by genealogy in their villages, whom David and Samuel the seer ordained in their office of trust.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: and didn’t inquire of the LORD. Therefore he killed him, and turned the kingdom over to David the son of Jesse.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: Then all Israel gathered themselves to David to Hebron, saying, “Behold, we are your bone and your flesh.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: So all the elders of Israel came to the king to Hebron; and David made a covenant with them in Hebron before the LORD. They anointed David king over Israel, according to the LORD’s word by Samuel.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: David and all Israel went to Jerusalem (also called Jebus); and the Jebusites, the inhabitants of the land, were there.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: The inhabitants of Jebus said to David, “You will not come in here!” Nevertheless David took the stronghold of Zion. The same is David’s city.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: David had said, “Whoever strikes the Jebusites first shall be chief and captain.” Joab the son of Zeruiah went up first, and was made chief.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: David lived in the stronghold; therefore they called it David’s city.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: David grew greater and greater, for the LORD of Armies was with him.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: Now these are the chief of the mighty men whom David had, who showed themselves strong with him in his kingdom, together with all Israel, to make him king, according to the LORD’s word concerning Israel.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: This is the number of the mighty men whom David had: Jashobeam, the son of a Hachmonite, the chief of the thirty; he lifted up his spear against three hundred and killed them at one time.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: He was with David at Pasdammim, and there the Philistines were gathered together to battle, where there was a plot of ground full of barley; and the people fled from before the Philistines.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: Three of the thirty chief men went down to the rock to David, into the cave of Adullam; and the army of the Philistines were encamped in the valley of Rephaim.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: David was then in the stronghold, and the garrison of the Philistines was in Bethlehem at that time.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: David longed, and said, “Oh, that someone would give me water to drink from the well of Bethlehem, which is by the gate!”
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: The three broke through the army of the Philistines, and drew water out of the well of Bethlehem that was by the gate, took it, and brought it to David; but David would not drink any of it, but poured it out to the LORD,
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: Behold, he was more honorable than the thirty, but he didn’t attain to the three; and David set him over his guard.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: Now these are those who came to David to Ziklag while he was a fugitive from Saul the son of Kish. They were among the mighty men, his helpers in war.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: Some Gadites joined David in the stronghold in the wilderness, mighty men of valor, men trained for war, who could handle shield and spear; whose faces were like the faces of lions, and they were as swift as the gazelles on the mountains:
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: Some of the children of Benjamin and Judah came to the stronghold to David.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: David went out to meet them, and answered them, “If you have come peaceably to me to help me, my heart will be united with you; but if you have come to betray me to my adversaries, since there is no wrong in my hands, may the God of our fathers see this and rebuke it.”
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: Then the Spirit came on Amasai, who was chief of the thirty, and he said, “We are yours, David, and on your side, you son of Jesse. Peace, peace be to you, and peace be to your helpers; for your God helps you.” Then David received them and made them captains of the band.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: Some of Manasseh also joined David when he came with the Philistines against Saul to battle, but they didn’t help them, for the lords of the Philistines sent him away after consultation, saying, “He will desert to his master Saul to the jeopardy of our heads.”
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: They helped David against the band of raiders, for they were all mighty men of valor and were captains in the army.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: For from day to day men came to David to help him, until there was a great army, like God’s army.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: These are the numbers of the heads of those who were armed for war, who came to David to Hebron to turn the kingdom of Saul to him, according to the LORD’s word.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: Of the half-tribe of Manasseh: eighteen thousand, who were mentioned by name, to come and make David king.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: All these were men of war who could order the battle array, and came with a perfect heart to Hebron to make David king over all Israel; and all the rest also of Israel were of one heart to make David king.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: They were there with David three days, eating and drinking; for their brothers had supplied provisions for them.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: David consulted with the captains of thousands and of hundreds, even with every leader.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: David said to all the assembly of Israel, “If it seems good to you, and if it is of the LORD our God, let’s send word everywhere to our brothers who are left in all the land of Israel, with whom the priests and Levites are in their cities that have pasture lands, that they may gather themselves to us.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: So David assembled all Israel together, from the Shihor River of Egypt even to the entrance of Hamath, to bring God’s ark from Kiriath Jearim.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: David went up with all Israel to Baalah, that is, to Kiriath Jearim, which belonged to Judah, to bring up from there God the LORD’s ark that sits above the cherubim, that is called by the Name.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: David and all Israel played before God with all their might, even with songs, with harps, with stringed instruments, with tambourines, with cymbals, and with trumpets.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: David was displeased, because the LORD had broken out against Uzza. He called that place Perez Uzza, to this day.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: David was afraid of God that day, saying, “How can I bring God’s ark home to me?”
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: So David didn’t move the ark with him into David’s city, but carried it aside into Obed-Edom the Gittite’s house.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: Hiram king of Tyre sent messengers to David with cedar trees, masons, and carpenters, to build him a house.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: David perceived that the LORD had established him king over Israel, for his kingdom was highly exalted, for his people Israel’s sake.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: David took more wives in Jerusalem, and David became the father of more sons and daughters.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: When the Philistines heard that David was anointed king over all Israel, all the Philistines went up to seek David; and David heard of it, and went out against them.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: David inquired of God, saying, “Shall I go up against the Philistines? Will you deliver them into my hand?” The LORD said to him, “Go up; for I will deliver them into your hand.”
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: So they came up to Baal Perazim, and David defeated them there. David said, God has broken my enemies by my hand, like waters breaking out. Therefore they called the name of that place Baal Perazim.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: They left their gods there; and David gave a command, and they were burned with fire.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: David inquired again of God; and God said to him, “You shall not go up after them. Turn away from them, and come on them opposite the mulberry trees.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: David did as God commanded him; and they attacked the army of the Philistines from Gibeon even to Gezer.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: The fame of David went out into all lands; and the LORD brought the fear of him on all nations.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: David made himself houses in David’s city; and he prepared a place for God’s ark, and pitched a tent for it.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: Then David said, “No one ought to carry God’s ark but the Levites. For the LORD has chosen them to carry God’s ark, and to minister to him forever.”
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: David assembled all Israel at Jerusalem, to bring up the LORD’s ark to its place, which he had prepared for it.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: David gathered together the sons of Aaron and the Levites:
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: David called for Zadok and Abiathar the priests, and for the Levites: for Uriel, Asaiah, Joel, Shemaiah, Eliel, and Amminadab,
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: David spoke to the chief of the Levites to appoint their brothers as singers with instruments of music, stringed instruments, harps, and cymbals, sounding aloud and lifting up their voices with joy.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: So David, the elders of Israel, and the captains over thousands went to bring the ark of the LORD’s covenant up out of the house of Obed-Edom with joy.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: David was clothed with a robe of fine linen, as were all the Levites who bore the ark, the singers, and Chenaniah the choir master with the singers; and David had an ephod of linen on him.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: As the ark of the LORD’s covenant came to David’s city, Michal the daughter of Saul looked out at the window, and saw king David dancing and playing; and she despised him in her heart.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: They brought in God’s ark, and set it in the middle of the tent that David had pitched for it; and they offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before God.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: When David had finished offering the burnt offering and the peace offerings, he blessed the people in the LORD’s name.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: Then on that day David first ordained giving of thanks to the LORD by the hand of Asaph and his brothers.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: All the people departed, each man to his house; and David returned to bless his house.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: When David was living in his house, David said to Nathan the prophet, “Behold, I live in a cedar house, but the ark of the LORD’s covenant is in a tent.”
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: Nathan said to David, “Do all that is in your heart; for God is with you.”
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: “Go and tell David my servant, ‘The LORD says, “You shall not build me a house to dwell in;
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: “Now therefore, you shall tell my servant David, ‘The LORD of Armies says, “I took you from the sheep pen, from following the sheep, to be prince over my people Israel.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: According to all these words, and according to all this vision, so Nathan spoke to David.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: Then David the king went in and sat before the LORD; and he said, “Who am I, LORD God, and what is my house, that you have brought me this far?
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: What can David say yet more to you concerning the honor which is done to your servant? For you know your servant.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: Let your name be established and magnified forever, saying, ‘The LORD of Armies is the God of Israel, even a God to Israel. The house of David your servant is established before you.’
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: After this, David defeated the Philistines and subdued them, and took Gath and its towns out of the hand of the Philistines.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: He defeated Moab; and the Moabites became servants to David and brought tribute.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: David defeated Hadadezer king of Zobah, toward Hamath, as he went to establish his dominion by the river Euphrates.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: David took from him one thousand chariots, seven thousand horsemen, and twenty thousand footmen; and David hamstrung all the chariot horses, but reserved of them enough for one hundred chariots.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: When the Syrians of Damascus came to help Hadadezer king of Zobah, David struck twenty-two thousand men of the Syrians.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: Then David put garrisons in Syria of Damascus; and the Syrians became servants to David and brought tribute. The LORD gave victory to David wherever he went.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: David took the shields of gold that were on the servants of Hadadezer, and brought them to Jerusalem.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: From Tibhath and from Cun, cities of Hadadezer, David took very much bronze, with which Solomon made the bronze sea, the pillars, and the vessels of bronze.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: When Tou king of Hamath heard that David had struck all the army of Hadadezer king of Zobah,
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: he sent Hadoram his son to King David to greet him and to bless him, because he had fought against Hadadezer and struck him (for Hadadezer had wars with Tou); and he had with him all kinds of vessels of gold and silver and bronze.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: King David also dedicated these to the LORD, with the silver and the gold that he carried away from all the nations: from Edom, from Moab, from the children of Ammon, from the Philistines, and from Amalek.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: He put garrisons in Edom; and all the Edomites became servants to David. The LORD gave victory to David wherever he went.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: David reigned over all Israel; and he executed justice and righteousness for all his people.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was over the Cherethites and the Pelethites; and the sons of David were chief officials serving the king.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: David said, “I will show kindness to Hanun the son of Nahash, because his father showed kindness to me.” So David sent messengers to comfort him concerning his father. David’s servants came into the land of the children of Ammon to Hanun to comfort him.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: But the princes of the children of Ammon said to Hanun, “Do you think that David honors your father, in that he has sent comforters to you? Haven’t his servants come to you to search, to overthrow, and to spy out the land?”
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: So Hanun took David’s servants, shaved them, and cut off their garments in the middle at their buttocks, and sent them away.
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: Then some people went and told David how the men were treated. He sent to meet them; for the men were greatly humiliated. The king said, “Stay at Jericho until your beards have grown, and then return.”
sourceChecks.readingNoteJa: 固定WEBの各候補箇所を原文と前後の系譜文脈で確認。

sourceChecks.text: When the children of Ammon saw that they had made themselves odious to David, Hanun and the children of Ammon sent one thousand talents of silver to hire chariots and horsemen out of Mesopotamia, out of Aram-maacah, and out of Zobah.
